title: Differentially private tests of Fisher's sharp null hypothesis for binary outcomes

split.decision: Independent two-sided geometric privatized releases, 36 cells x1000 per split; shuffled opaque IDs; raw counts and truth excluded from inputs.

baseline.paper_ref: Historical mean width 0.3876; no full reference measured for this conversion.

allowed_changes: Posterior sampling, exact enumeration, integration, caching of input-independent calculations and other numerical approximation may change.
Draw count and numerical routines may improve; auxiliary losses must approximate the same posterior rather than create a different uncertainty set.
When retaining the supplied DP-FRT-Bayes sampler, changing only R=10000 or method='sampling' does not count as a method improvement.
fixed_contract: Compute the central 95% credible set of the nonprivate Fisher randomization p-value under the specified DP-FRT-Bayes denoising posterior, minimizing its guarded width.
The discrete uniform prior over valid treated/control count pairs and two-sided geometric privacy likelihood with supplied epsilon define the fixed posterior.

The Fisher hypergeometric right-tail p-value, central 2.5%/97.5% posterior quantiles and supported discrete set between them, 12-decimal membership, 36-cell width/coverage rules and privatized inputs remain fixed.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
method_freedom_review.budget_policy: agent overall deadline; separate overall formal replay budget
forbidden_substitutions: Do not change the count prior, privacy likelihood or p-value tail; replace credible sets with arbitrary frequentist intervals/HPD sets; or choose case-specific answers.
No original counts, latent noise, hidden case labels or additional privacy releases may be used.
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.
